rv.q: Thanks to Central Square Theater’s production of Eleanor , a riveting one-woman show starring Paula Plum, Eleanor Roosevelt comes to life as a fully-fledged, accomplished woman with an inner life to match her outer one.

Precise direction from Bryn Boice allows the intricate script to progress with clarity, presenting a finely woven tapestry of events and reflections that dramatize a life devoted to public service and marked by acts of courage over the course of ninety intermission-free minutes.
Eleanor is a fascinating, educational, inspiring and enriching biographical memory play helmed by Paula Plum’s tremendous performance as Eleanor.
Eleanor’s strength, intellect and work to make the world better for women and historically marginalized groups are worthy of being remembered.
This play often comes across as calculated and obligatory, as if the playwright was checking the boxes required for a biographical drama.
